title: NO FAT FROM CATTLE, SHEEP, OR GOATS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The LORD said to Moses, 'Say to the Israelites: "Do not eat any of the fat of cattle, sheep or goats. The fat of an animal found dead or torn by wild animals may be used for any other purpose, but you must not eat it."'" - Lev 7:22-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The fat belonged to God. That was established back in chapter 3: all the fat is the LORD's.

So Israel could not eat the fat of the three sacrificial animals — cattle, sheep, goats — even when the animal was slaughtered at home for an ordinary family meal. The restriction reached into every kitchen.

Why? Because a boundary that only applies at the tabernacle is not really a boundary. God was training a whole nation to recognise that some things are simply not theirs to take, wherever they are and whoever is watching.

That is the heart of integrity. Not behaving well in the sanctuary, but behaving consistently at home, where no priest could see.

Interestingly, God permitted other uses for the fat of an animal found dead. It could be used for lamp oil, soap, leather-working. God was not being arbitrarily restrictive. He drew a specific line and left everything else free.

These particular food laws are not binding on believers today (Mk 7:19; Acts 10:15). But the principle behind them is permanent: God's people live by His boundaries even when nobody is checking.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I the same person in private that I am in public?
2. Is there a boundary I keep at church and quietly ignore at home?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, make me consistent. Let my private life match what I profess when others are watching. Amen.
